answer.answer: Straylight is not ready for dependable owner use at projected scale. The newer current-status note controls and explicitly supersedes the older green checkpoint, whose results predate the production-sized timeout and full-manifest-copy findings. The approved redesign direction is documented but not yet verified as implemented.

claims.value: Projects/Straylight current status.md, updated 2026-07-26T12:00:00-07:00, controls because it explicitly supersedes Projects/Straylight stale checkpoint.md. The stale checkpoint was recorded 2026-07-23T18:00:00-07:00; its passing retrieval test corpus, healthy `/ready` configuration, and immediate owner-alpha proposal are historical evidence that must not override the newer production findings.

Connection and authentication work, and exact-path reads work, but broad `memory.open` and lexical retrieval are slow and can hit the 30-second database timeout. Retrieval lanes share one transaction, so a later lane failure can cause an earlier successful lane to be lost. Consequently, current retrieval is not dependable for owner use despite the older green test result.

Normal writes copy a full corpus membership manifest. With about 64,000 active records and 9.6 million estimated source tokens already present, this write amplification contributes to an architecture that is not ready for dependable owner use at 10x corpus growth.

The approved simplification is to make current Markdown files the workspace truth; version only changed files; make indexes and derived views rebuildable; checkpoint using exact path, version, and hash references plus changes since a workspace generation; and retain coherent source hydration and compact retrieval packets. This is the approved direction, not evidence of completed or production-verified implementation.
